question: Of 10 products, 4 are defective. If 3 are drawn without replacement, what is the probability that all 3 are defective?

provenance.contribution: Existing attributed explanation retained; project contribution is review and annotations.
provenance.reviewStatus: Current explanation retained and independently AI-reviewed; not teacher reviewed

solutionMethods.explanation:
For uniform random sampling without replacement, all three items are defective exactly when each successive draw is defective. After each such draw, one defective item and one item overall have been removed, so the successive probabilities are \(\frac4{10}\), \(\frac39\), and \(\frac28\). By the probability multiplication rule,
\[
P(\text{all three defective})
=\frac4{10}\cdot\frac39\cdot\frac28
=\frac1{30}.
\]
solutionMethods.label: Multiply successive defective-draw probabilities
